correctness.rationale: The max-of-eight-support-functionals octagonal norm and the constraints N(x)=N(y)=N(x-y)=1 reduce to 8^3 ordered edge triples. Each feasible rank-two affine intersection is an interval; convexity makes every shifted norm attain its maximum at an endpoint. The inspected Q(sqrt(2)) verifier handles exact interval endpoints/support changes and reports 48 feasible families and 128 checked breakpoints. An independently coded numerical re-enumeration (all 512 triples) confirmed 48 feasible rank-two families, the exact predicted bound to floating tolerance, and no counterexamples; 32 rank-one triples have all parallel supporting edges and cannot be equilateral because a common norming functional of x-y would be in {-2,0,2} rather than +/-1. Independently checked explicit witness x=(1,sqrt(2)-1),y=(3-2sqrt(2),1) satisfies all three unit constraints and both shifted norms equal 2sqrt(2)-1. These finite checks are exhaustive only because of the proven convex-polyhedral reduction; numerical replay is corroboration, not sole proof.
residual_risks: Unverified publisher/Lean/expert certification is not asserted; exact scope is only the stated hypothesis.
